findings.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:7 uses `<%- end if %>`, which ERB compiles to a bare `end if` with no condition — a Ruby syntax error that opens a never-closed conditional, so the template fails to compile and embed#best raises ActionView::Template::Error on the topic-found success path (first request renders the loading page, then 500s forever after the 30s reload); rspec-rails 2.x controller specs don't render views so CI stays green while the feature is broken in production. Fix: `<%- end %>`.

Stored XSS: RSS/Atom feed content is imported and served completely unsanitized — poll_feed.rb feeds raw item HTML to topic_embed.rb which sets cook_method: raw_html, post.rb's cook returns raw verbatim with no sanitize pipeline, and it is rendered via `raw post.cooked` in best.html.erb:23 and as `cooked` throughout the forum UI; anyone who publishes, compromises, or MITMs the feed (fetched over plain `open()`) can execute arbitrary script on the Discourse origin and steal viewer sessions.
The import_remote readability path whitelists tags but not URL schemes, so `<a href='javascript:...'>` survives sanitization as an additional live XSS vector.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 interpolates `url` unescaped into a single-quoted href after only a prefix check (`url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`); URLs legally containing a single quote (e.g. slugs like `/it's-alive.html`) terminate the attribute early and corrupt the stored HTML, and a crafted feed link such as `http://host/x' onmouseover='...` performs attribute injection that lands as live markup since the post is raw_html-cooked (second XSS path).

topic_embed.rb:31-34 update path assumes embed.post is non-nil when passing it to PostRevisor.new; nothing removes topic_embeds rows when a topic/post is destroyed, so an orphaned embed makes PostRevisor#initialize NoMethodError mid-loop inside poll_feed's rss.items.each with retry: false — every feed item after the orphaned one is never imported every hour and the embed request for that URL fails persistently, silently degrading the feed import.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:26-29: $redis.setnx and $redis.expire are not atomic; if the process dies between them the retrieved:<url> key has no TTL and lives forever, permanently throttling that embed URL so perform_retrieve never runs again and the page shows 'Loading Discussion...' indefinitely. Use a single `SET ... EX 60 NX`.

topic_embed.rb:64-76 (absolutize_urls) mangles protocol-relative URLs: `//cdn.example.com/img.jpg` passes `start_with?('/')` and then `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both leading slashes, producing `http://<embed host>/cdn.example.com/img.jpg` — a broken path on the wrong host, breaking images/links in imported posts.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17: the origin check is substring-based (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`) rather than exact equality, so any origin that is a substring-prefix of the forum URL (e.g. `http://fo` matching `http://forum.example.com`) can post discourse-resize messages and drive the iframe height arbitrarily; the check should be `e.origin === discourseUrl`.

embed_controller.rb:9-16 / topic_retriever.rb:15-18: embed_url is never validated as a String — params.require(:embed_url) happily returns an Array/Hash (`?embed_url[]=x`), and URI(@embed_url) in invalid_host? raises TypeError (not URI::InvalidURIError) which escapes the rescue, so each such request enqueues a job that crashes on its first statement and burns through Sidekiq retries — anonymous-triggerable job churn. Validate it's a String before enqueueing.

embed_controller.rb: the referer gate relies on the spoofable, fully client-controlled request.referer header, so it stops browsers but not scripted callers; any request with a faked referer and a novel embed_url enqueues RetrieveTopic, and with feed_polling_enabled each such job synchronously re-polls and re-parses the entire feed (Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})) plus a readability fetch — enabling anonymous queue-flooding / forced-feed-refresh amplification. A global rate limit on the controller is needed.

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:143: the importer rewrite from PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id) to TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title]) silently drops both timestamps and category support — imported Disqus topics are dated 'now' (reordering listing pages and breaking embed dates), always land in uncategorized, and the -c CLI option was removed; import_remote should at least forward created_at.

Unbounded feed processing in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29-37: the poll fetches and parses the entire feed and iterates every item with no item cap, batching, or delta detection, so every hour is a full O(feed_size) re-scan (SHA-1 over each item's full content plus a TopicEmbed.import per item) regardless of changes; the first poll on a large/archival feed imports the whole feed in a single Sidekiq execution, and work and DB write amplification scale linearly with feed size with no bound.

The feed_key helper (poll_feed.rb:20-21, the vestigial 'feed-modified' key) is dead code: conditional-fetch/If-Modified-Since support was never wired up, so there is no change detection on the feed poll.

N+1 query pattern in the feed loop: TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first (app/models/topic_embed.rb:15) is called per item from poll_feed.rb:36, plus a lazy embed.post load at :32 and TopicEmbed.where(...).exists? at lib/topic_retriever.rb:37 and :42 — one indexed SELECT per feed item every hour even when nothing changed; a single batched where(embed_url: urls) returning a lookup hash would collapse this to one query per poll.

Retrieving a single embed URL synchronously executes the entire feed poll: lib/topic_retriever.rb:40-43 calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) inline, so M distinct un-imported URLs (each with its own 60s throttle key at :21-33) trigger M full feed polls, uncoordinated with the hourly schedule — on initial embed rollout that means one full fetch+scan per page view.
There is no mutex between the scheduled and inline poll paths, and if the inline poll runs longer than the 60s throttle TTL, concurrent jobs re-enter and duplicate the work.

Unbounded remote download into memory with no size/time policy: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 (open(url).read) and poll_feed.rb:29 buffer the full remote body into a String and parse it (readability + Nokogiri, several times the document size in memory) with no max-size cap, bounded only by open-uri's default 60s timeouts; any large resource served on the embeddable_host will be fully downloaded and parsed in a Sidekiq worker.

No enqueue-time dedupe and no negative caching on the retrieve path (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15, app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:8-10, lib/topic_retriever.rb:21-33): every embed impression enqueues a job, so a page whose topic can never be imported floods the Sidekiq queue with near-duplicate jobs whose only work is a failed setnx; the 60s throttle only applies inside job execution and is set before retrieval regardless of outcome, so permanently failing URLs (404, readability-empty, fetch error) are re-fetched up to once per minute indefinitely as long as they have viewers.
The Redis setnx/expire throttle operations are non-atomic: a crash between them throttles that URL forever.

TopicView may not honor {best: 5} or exclude the first post (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13, app/views/embed/best.html.erb:12-27): the PR makes no change to TopicView and the controller spec only stubs it (TopicView.expects(:new)), so nothing proves this revision supports the best option; if best is ignored, the embed view renders every post in the topic with no pagination (response size and render cost grow unboundedly with comment count), and the imported article's potentially very large raw HTML (cook_method: raw_html, echoed via raw post.cooked) could be dumped into the iframe. Needs verification; P1 if unsupported.

No nil guard for feed items lacking a content/content:encoded element (common in RSS 2.0 feeds): CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) at app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 raises NoMethodError on nil.scrub; with retry: false at :12 and items processed in feed order, everything after the bad item never imports and re-fails every hour, and because perform_retrieve runs the poll inline, the exception also aborts retrieve_topic before fetch_http ever runs — so new embed URLs stop importing entirely while the bad item exists.
String#scrub availability on the deployment Ruby (2.1+) should be spot-checked.

force: true was added to the already-shipped migration db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — inert day-to-day since normal deploys skip recorded migrations, but any db:migrate:redo or reset against an environment with data silently drops top_tables... top_topics; reads like a local-dev convenience accidentally committed, and the same pattern in the brand-new create_topic_embeds migration (20131217174004) sets a bad precedent.

External HTML from polled RSS/ATOM feeds and readability extraction of arbitrary embeddable-host pages is stored and served completely unsanitized, causing stored XSS in the Discourse origin for every visitor of every embedding third-party page: the `cook_method == raw_html` early return in app/models/post.rb:133 bypasses the entire cooking/sanitization pipeline (Sanitize), app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35-36 imports `i.content` raw with zero sanitization, and app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 renders it via `raw post.cooked`

HTML attribute injection via unescaped URL interpolation in app/models/topic_embed.rb:13: `url` is interpolated into `<a href='#{url}'>` without escaping, so a URL like `http://host/x' onmouseover='...` (single quotes are legal URIs and pass the http(s) URL check) yields attribute injection

Public CLI signature break: the `--category/-c` option was removed from the Disqus import task (lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117) and the category is no longer passed to PostCreator (:144), so existing callers invoking `disqus:import -c` abort with an unknown-option error and imported topics all land in Uncategorized; output also drifts to full readability-extracted HTML plus a TopicEmbed row instead of a permalink stub, which can later collide with feed-polling imports keyed on the same URL

SSRF via redirect: the host allowlist is checked only on the initial URL (lib/topic_retriever.rb:15), but the actual fetches via `open-uri` (app/models/topic_embed.rb:36, app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29) follow cross-origin redirects, so an open redirect on the embeddable host can pivot the Discourse server to fetch internal endpoints (169.254.169.254, localhost services) whose content is then readable via the public topic/embed; the referer gate is a forgeable header, so no on-host presence is even needed to trigger retrieval
No fetch timeout or size cap is set on the `open()` fetches, so retrieval/poll jobs can be hung or OOM'd

PollFeed crashes on common RSS 2.0 feeds: `i.content.scrub` at app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 raises NoMethodError because SimpleRSS exposes RSS 2.0's `content:encoded` as `content_encoded` and plain RSS items have no `content`; with `sidekiq_options retry: false` (:12) the hourly import dies mid-feed and items after the crash point are never imported, silently breaking the documented RSS/ATOM support for the most common feeds (WordPress et al.); `String#scrub` also requires Ruby >= 2.1

`absolutize_urls` corrupts protocol-relative URLs: the `href.start_with?('/')` check at app/models/topic_embed.rb:61-72 treats `//cdn.example.com/img.png` as a root-relative path and, after stripping leading slashes, produces `http://<embeddable-host>/cdn.example.com/img.png`, breaking links and images in every feed containing `//` URLs

`<%- end if %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 is not a block terminator — it either fails to compile (template SyntaxError making every successful /embed/best render a 500) or parses as a bizarre modifier-if whose condition is the next emitted ERB output, making the header block depend on unrelated template code; it should be `<%- end -%>`, and since the controller specs stub TopicView and never render views, the breakage would ship undetected

Embed URL matching is a byte-exact string contract across three independently produced values — the stored `embed_url` (app/models/topic_embed.rb:78-80), the client snippet's `discourseEmbedUrl` (app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7), and the feed's `i.link` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:32) — with no normalization layer anywhere, so any divergence (trailing slash, scheme, www, query params) means the embed never matches and the user sees the loading page reloading every 30s indefinitely while the server re-enqueues retrievals

The `retrieve_topic` job is enqueued before any validation of user input (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15) — the host allowlist runs only later inside the job (lib/topic_retriever.rb:15) and the referer gate is a forgeable header, so an anonymous client with a forged `Referer: http://<embeddable-host>/` can enqueue unbounded jobs (varying embed_url to bypass the per-URL throttle), and each first-time retrieval synchronously re-runs the entire feed import inline

Referer-based gating (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26) fails for referer-less clients: browsers/extensions configured to suppress the Referer header (private modes, privacy tools) render a hard error inside the embed iframe instead of comments

The `embeddable_host` setting is silently config-sensitive: it must be a bare host string — an admin entering `https://example.com` or a host with a port never string-matches `URI(...).host`, and the feature fails silently with no validation or documentation of the expected format

Plugin hook contract regression: the early `return raw` at app/models/post.rb:133 happens before `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`, so documented plugin cook-pipeline filters (link rewriting, nofollow injection, content filtering) are silently skipped for raw HTML posts with no opt-out or documentation

Already-shipped migration edited and given `force: true`: `create_table :top_topics, force: true` in db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 drops the table if it exists when the migration runs, violating released-migration immutability and risking silent data loss in environments where the table exists without the schema_migrations entry (partial states, restored dumps)

`{best: 5}` passed to TopicView (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13) is not implemented anywhere in this diff — if TopicView ignores unknown options, the /embed/best endpoint serves default/latest posts rather than 'best' ones, and the specs only verify the call signature (not that the option does anything), so it ships unverified

PollFeed's `rss.items.each` loop has no begin/rescue around `TopicEmbed.import`, so a single bad feed item (nil field, bad URL, PostCreator failure, RecordNotUnique race) permanently poisons all feed importing — the job aborts, and with `retry: false` and hourly scheduling the next run dies on the same item, so later items are never imported; the unused `feed_key` also leaves no way to skip or flag a bad feed.

`TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` runs the entire feed poll inline in every retrieve job with no lock: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` fetches and imports the whole feed synchronously once per unique embed_url per 60s, effectively DDoS-ing the embeddable host, racing the check-then-insert in `TopicEmbed.import` into `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` exceptions, and failing retrieve jobs on any PollFeed failure.

External feed content is stored and served as unsanitized raw HTML: the RSS path has no sanitization at all before content becomes `cooked`, the readability path whitelists tags but permits `javascript:` URLs in href/src attributes, and the feed-supplied URL is interpolated unescaped into HTML — a malicious or hijacked feed yields stored script running on the Discourse origin.

Outbound HTTP calls (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and `open(url).read`) have no explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`, no redirect policy, and no response-size cap, so a slow feed server ties up Sidekiq workers and a huge response is slurped wholesale into memory before being persisted with no post-length bound.

`/embed/best` enqueues a `RetrieveTopic` background job on every request with no rate limiting — the Referer host check in `ensure_embeddable` is a client-controlled, trivially spoofed header, so varying the `embed_url` param generates unbounded queue growth; the 60s Redis throttle limits fetch frequency, not enqueue volume.

No lifecycle cleanup for `topic_embeds`: nothing deletes a TopicEmbed when its topic or post is deleted, leaving a stale topic_id that makes `TopicView.new` 404, permanently blocking re-creation for that URL because `perform_retrieve` short-circuits on the existing embed, and causing a `NoMethodError` when `PostRevisor.new(post)` receives a nil post.

The embed loading page reloads forever with no failure state or retry cap, and failure is silent on both client and operator side: retrieval silently no-ops when `embed_by_username` is unset or the user was deleted, when the host doesn't match, or when retrieval fails, and no poll/retrieve path logs anything — with no circuit breaker, a permanently-bad embed URL is re-fetched once a minute indefinitely.

Feed item parsing assumes `i.content` exists, but simple-rss exposes namespaced `content:encoded` as `content_encoded`, so RSS 2.0 description-only feeds raise `NoMethodError` on `i.content.scrub`, and combined with the missing error isolation one such item kills the entire poll.

`String#scrub` requires Ruby ≥ 2.1 but these migrations are dated to the pre-Ruby-2.1 deployment era and the `string-scrub` gem was not added to the Gemfile, so on a runtime lacking it every poll raises on the first item and feed importing never works at all.

Migration `add_cook_method_to_posts` uses `ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT ... NOT NULL`, which on PostgreSQL < 11 rewrites the `posts` table while holding an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, causing minutes of total post-query lockout during deploy on busy forums.

The `setnx`/`expire` throttle in `TopicRetriever` is not atomic: if the worker dies between the two calls, the `retrieved:<url>` key persists with no TTL and that URL is throttled permanently until manual Redis intervention; should use `set(key, "1", nx: true, ex: 60)`.

`import_remote` fetches the URL before validating its scheme: `open(url)` executes before the `^https?://` check in `import`, so a schemeless string like `//eviltrout.com/x` passes `invalid_host?` and hits `Kernel#open`'s local-file semantics instead of HTTP.

`<%- end if %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` is a typo (presumably meant `<%- end %>`) that only renders correctly by accident of ERB's chunk emission order, and is one template edit away from a semantics change or a `SyntaxError` that breaks every embed render with a topic present.

`create_table ..., force: true` in production migrations (`create_topic_embeds`, `create_top_topics`) can silently drop any pre-existing table without warning if the migration is re-run, and modifying the already-shipped `CreateTopTopics` migration is a no-op on already-migrated databases that only adds risk.

The Disqus import loop now performs network I/O with no rescue: `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)` inside `parser.threads.each` means a single 404 or timeout on an old export permalink aborts the entire CLI run partway through.

Jobs::PollFeed's core feed-to-topic pipeline has zero behavioral coverage: the spec stubs poll_feed itself, so SimpleRSS parsing, the link fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), the missing-user early return, and the handoff to TopicEmbed.import are never executed, and no test anywhere verifies a feed item produces a topic/post. This untested path hides a latent crash: i.content.scrub (poll_feed.rb:35) raises NoMethodError on feeds/items lacking a content element (common in plain RSS 2.0 feeds with only <description>), and since the job is sidekiq_options retry: false, it dies silently every hour.

Imported HTML is served completely unsanitized: Post#cook returns raw verbatim for cook_method: raw_html, bypassing the cooking/sanitization pipeline and the Plugin::Filter :after_post_cook hooks. PollFeed passes raw feed HTML straight into this path (only the readability path whitelists tags), and the embed view renders it with raw post.cooked (and it renders unsanitized on the regular topic page too) — a crafted feed/article containing <script> or onerror= executes in the Discourse origin for every viewer, including logged-in users. The spec (topic_embed_spec.rb:29 asserting cooked == raw) codifies the vulnerability instead of guarding against it.

The three PollFeed guard tests (spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:12-30) pass for the wrong reason: each stubs only one setting and leaves the others at their real defaults (feed_polling_enabled: false, feed_polling_url: '', embed_by_username: '') which already make the poll_feed condition false — e.g. 'requires feed_polling_url' leaves feed_polling_enabled? at default false so the first conjunct short-circuits. Deleting any single gating condition would not fail any spec; each test should set the other two settings to valid values so only the condition under test can fail.

Every meaningful behavior of TopicRetriever is mocked in its own spec: all tests stub either perform_retrieve or retrieved_recently?, so the only real code exercised is the host comparison. The 60-second $redis.setnx/expire throttle and perform_retrieve's logic (bail if embed exists, run Jobs::PollFeed first when enabled, fetch_http's user lookup) have no coverage — a typo in the redis key, a dropped expire, or removing the exists?-check would not fail any spec.

The embed controller's success-path tests verify mock interactions, not behavior: 'Tells the topic retriever to work' asserts TopicRetriever.new/retrieve are called instead of asserting Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) args, and TopicRetriever.expects(:new) matches any arguments; 'Creates a topic view' mocks TopicView.new returning nil. With view rendering off, nothing verifies the best template renders posts or that the loading template renders on the no-embed path — a broken template (e.g. @topic_view.posts on a stale/deleted topic id) ships green. No render_views/integration spec exists for either new template.

TopicEmbed.import_remote has no tests despite becoming the backbone of TopicRetriever#fetch_http and the rewritten disqus importer (disqus.thor switched from PostCreator to TopicEmbed.import_remote): readability extraction (title extraction, tag/attribute whitelist, opts[:title] override) is never exercised, nor is failure handling — open(url) on a 404 raises inside the job with nothing asserting behavior. Any bug in extraction now silently breaks two features.

'is 404 without an embed_url' (embed_controller_spec.rb:8-11) never reaches params.require and passes for the wrong reason: with no stub, the real default embeddable_host is '' so ensure_embeddable raises before the action runs — the loose should_not be_success passes because of the blank host (and the status is 403, not 404). Deleting params.require(:embed_url) would not fail any test.

The TopicEmbed update test cannot detect if revision loses raw_html cooking: post.cooked =~ /new contents/ would also pass if PostRevisor cooked the new raw through the regular markdown pipeline (the phrase survives markdown), so nothing verifies cook_method is preserved across revision. Also untested: importing identical content triggers no revision (the content_sha1 guard and embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...)), and that update doesn't create a duplicate topic/embed (TopicEmbed.count == 1 never asserted).

absolutize_urls edge cases are untested, including a real mangling of protocol-relative URLs: //cdn.example.com/x starts with /, gets all leading slashes stripped by sub(/^\/+/, ''), and is rewritten to http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/x — a common real-world pattern that silently produces broken links. Port-bearing URLs (prefix << ":#{uri.port}") are also uncovered.

Jobs::RetrieveTopic (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:11-20) has no spec: the Discourse::InvalidParameters raise for missing embed_url, the user lookup, and the staff no_throttle: user.try(:staff?) bypass (which feeds the untested throttle in the TopicRetriever spec) are all unexercised.

embed.js has no tests, including its security-relevant origin check: the postMessage handler's origin validation is a substring check (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) which accepts any origin that is a prefix of the discourse URL (e.g. http://discourse.example.co passes when the URL is http://discourse.example.com). The check is untested and wrong, though impact is low (iframe height only). A qunit test asserting strict origin equality would have caught this.

PostRevisor's new save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) (lib/post_revisor.rb:85) has no direct test despite changing behavior for every revision: nothing asserts validations are actually skipped, and the only indirect coverage (the TopicEmbed update test) would pass with validate: true since the revised content is long enough to validate — flipping the flag logic fails no spec.

Stored XSS on the feed path: TopicEmbed.import stores third-party feed content with cook_method raw_html (Post#cook returns raw verbatim) and it is served as cooked HTML with no sanitization — poll_feed.rb uses CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) with zero tag/attribute filtering (not even the readability whitelist used in import_remote), and unescapeHTML actively re-decodes entity-encoded payloads; embed/best.html.erb renders raw post.cooked (and normal topic pages render it too), so any script/iframe tag in the configured feed becomes stored XSS executing on the Discourse origin — the feed path needs the same tag/attribute whitelist applied in import_remote

Unescaped URL interpolated into an href inside the model (app/models/topic_embed.rb:13): the anchor is built via string interpolation with href='#{url}' where url is only validated against an https?:// prefix regex, which permits single quotes, >, and attribute-injection sequences; attacker-influenced feed item links flowing into raw HTML can break out of the attribute — escape the URL or build the anchor via Nokogiri

Separation-of-concerns smell in app/models/topic_embed.rb: the model composes presentation HTML (the anchor footer with I18n) and mutates the contents argument via contents << — the footer decoration should be moved out of the model

TopicRetriever executes the scheduled PollFeed job inline per embed request (lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})), bypassing Sidekiq; because the throttle key is per embed URL (retrieved:#{@embed_url}) rather than per feed, a site with k embedded articles can trigger up to k full feed fetches plus N import attempts per minute instead of the intended hourly poll, and any PollFeed exception now also fails RetrieveTopic with its retries re-polling the feed — this job-layer coupling should be an enqueue or a check against cached feed data, not an inline execute

Inverted layering: app/models/topic_embed.rb:44-53 (import_remote) performs the HTTP fetching (open(url).read) and HTML extraction (Readability::Document) inside the TopicEmbed ActiveRecord model while TopicRetriever only throttles and delegates, coupling the model to open-uri and the readability gem, making model specs require network stubs, and mixing persistence concerns with scraping — fetching/parsing belongs in TopicRetriever or a dedicated parser object, and TopicEmbed.import should be pure persistence/import logic

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 crashes with NoMethodError on any feed item lacking content (i.content.scrub when <content:encoded>/<content> is missing, very common in plain RSS 2.0), aborting the whole hourly poll mid-import; with sidekiq_options retry: false the failure is silent until the next hour — guard for nil and either rescue per-item or handle missing content
String#scrub is Ruby >= 2.1 only — on the Ruby 2.0 runtime current at this date, every poll_feed poll raises; rely on a backported scrub or an alternative

Only Gemfile_rails4.lock regenerated: new gems (ruby-readability, guess_html_encoding, simple-rss) are added to the Gemfile but the sibling lockfile is now out of sync, so bundle install --deployment/CI for the other bundle fails and drifts

TopicView is called with a {best: 5} option (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13) that nothing in this PR implements; unknown options are silently ignored so the embed renders default (first) posts rather than 'Best of', and the controller spec only asserts the option is passed through so tests cannot catch it — either the TopicView change is missing from the PR or this is a dead flag

Unescaped request.referer interpolated into a JS string literal (app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11: parent.postMessage with '<%= request.referer %>') with no escape_javascript; a referer containing a quote breaks out of the string and can execute script inside the embed iframe on the forum origin — use j/escape_javascript

Malformed ERB at app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6: <%- end if %> is a bare if modifier with no condition that only compiles by accident (the ERB compiler happens to emit a next buffer-append statement the parser swallows as an always-truthy condition); under any codegen emitting a ; separator or code chunk next it becomes a template SyntaxError that would 500 every successful embed render — almost certainly intended <%- end -%>
Dead code: require_dependency 'email/sender' at app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1 is unused copied boilerplate

Dead code: feed_key at app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20-22 is never referenced — looks like an abandoned 'modified since' optimization, which explains why the feed is now re-fetched in full every time
Dead code: the embed.permalink translation added to config/locales/server.en.yml is never used

Duplication with drift risk: User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first is duplicated at poll_feed.rb:25 and topic_retriever.rb with inconsistent guards (poll_feed checks .present? first; fetch_http does not)
Duplication: the TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: ...) lookup is duplicated across embed_controller.rb:10, topic_embed.rb:15, and topic_retriever.rb:37/42
Duplication: absolutize_urls (topic_embed.rb:62-73) contains copy-pasted a/img processing loops

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: RSS/Atom feed content is imported and served completely unsanitized — poll_feed.rb feeds raw item HTML to topic_embed.rb which sets cook_method: raw_html, post.rb's cook returns raw verbatim with no sanitize pipeline, and it is rendered via `raw post.cooked` in best.html.erb:23 and as `cooked` throughout the forum UI; anyone who publishes, compromises, or MITMs the feed (fetched over plain `open()`) can execute arbitrary script on the Discourse origin and steal viewer sessions.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a raw-HTML import path that bypasses Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` parses a remote feed via `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and passes `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` directly into `TopicEmbed.import(...)` with no sanitization. `TopicEmbed.import` creates the post with `PostCreator.new(..., raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`. `Post#cook` then returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == :raw_html`, skipping the rendering pipeline. The embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), meaning any `<script>`/event-handler HTML from the feed becomes stored XSS on the Discourse origin. The feed is fetched via `open(...)` and can be plain HTTP depending on the setting, making compromise/MITM a realistic injection vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The import_remote readability path whitelists tags but not URL schemes, so `<a href='javascript:...'>` survives sanitization as an additional live XSS vector.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, `Readability::Document.new` is configured to allow `<a>` tags and the `href` attribute (`tags: ... a ...`, `attributes: %w[href src]`). The resulting `doc.content` is then imported as a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` explicitly returns `raw` for `:raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. Since the diff shows no URL-scheme filtering on `href`, a `javascript:` URL could remain in the stored/rendered HTML, creating an XSS vector when rendered (e.g. `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` uses `<%= raw post.cooked %>`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 interpolates `url` unescaped into a single-quoted href after only a prefix check (`url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`); URLs legally containing a single quote (e.g. slugs like `/it's-alive.html`) terminate the attribute early and corrupt the stored HTML, and a crafted feed link such as `http://host/x' onmouseover='...` performs attribute injection that lands as live markup since the post is raw_html-cooked (second XSS path).

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the diff appends `"#{url}"` into `contents` after only checking `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`. This does not prevent legal URLs containing a single quote or other attribute-breaking characters, so `href='...` can be terminated early and additional attributes/handlers injected. Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged, and the embed view renders with `raw post.cooked`, the injected HTML would be served as live markup (XSS/markup corruption).

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:31-34 update path assumes embed.post is non-nil when passing it to PostRevisor.new; nothing removes topic_embeds rows when a topic/post is destroyed, so an orphaned embed makes PostRevisor#initialize NoMethodError mid-loop inside poll_feed's rss.items.each with retry: false — every feed item after the orphaned one is never imported every hour and the embed request for that URL fails persistently, silently degrading the feed import.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the update branch does `post = embed.post` and then (when the content SHA changes) unconditionally calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` without guarding against `post` being nil. The diff introduces `topic_embeds` with `post_id`/`topic_id` columns but no `dependent: :destroy` on `belongs_to` and no foreign keys shown, so an orphaned `topic_embeds` row is possible if the post/topic is deleted outside this code. Jobs::PollFeed iterates `rss.items.each` and calls `TopicEmbed.import(...)` with no rescue; an exception would abort the loop/job, and the job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, making this a persistent failure mode for that poll run (and likely every hourly run until the orphan is removed).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:26-29: $redis.setnx and $redis.expire are not atomic; if the process dies between them the retrieved:<url> key has no TTL and lives forever, permanently throttling that embed URL so perform_retrieve never runs again and the page shows 'Loading Discussion...' indefinitely. Use a single `SET ... EX 60 NX`.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb `retrieved_recently?` uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes (or errors) after `setnx` but before `expire`, the `retrieved:<url>` key will persist without a TTL, causing `retrieved_recently?` to return true indefinitely and permanently throttling retrieval for that embed URL (leading to repeated 'loading' behavior in EmbedController when no TopicEmbed exists yet). A single atomic `SET key value NX EX 60` avoids this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:64-76 (absolutize_urls) mangles protocol-relative URLs: `//cdn.example.com/img.jpg` passes `start_with?('/')` and then `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both leading slashes, producing `http://<embed host>/cdn.example.com/img.jpg` — a broken path on the wrong host, breaking images/links in imported posts.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, both link and image rewriting treat any href/src that `start_with?('/')` as a path-relative URL and rewrite it to `#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}`. A protocol-relative URL like `//cdn.example.com/img.jpg` satisfies `start_with?('/')`, and `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both leading slashes, producing `http(s)://<embed host>/cdn.example.com/img.jpg`, which is incorrect and breaks the asset/link host. This behavior is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17: the origin check is substring-based (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`) rather than exact equality, so any origin that is a substring-prefix of the forum URL (e.g. `http://fo` matching `http://forum.example.com`) can post discourse-resize messages and drive the iframe height arbitrarily; the check should be `e.origin === discourseUrl`.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, the message handler allows events when `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) !== -1`. This is a substring check, so an origin that is a prefix of the forum URL (e.g., `https://forum.example.co` vs `https://forum.example.com/...`) would pass and could send `discourse-resize` messages to arbitrarily change the iframe height. The diff clearly introduces this weaker-than-origin-equality validation in `postMessageReceived`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb:9-16 / topic_retriever.rb:15-18: embed_url is never validated as a String — params.require(:embed_url) happily returns an Array/Hash (`?embed_url[]=x`), and URI(@embed_url) in invalid_host? raises TypeError (not URI::InvalidURIError) which escapes the rescue, so each such request enqueues a job that crashes on its first statement and burns through Sidekiq retries — anonymous-triggerable job churn. Validate it's a String before enqueueing.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` only enforces presence; Rails can return an Array/Hash for `?embed_url[]=x` (or nested params). That value is passed unchanged into `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)`. In `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, the code calls `URI(@embed_url).host` and rescues only `URI::InvalidURIError`; if `@embed_url` is an Array/Hash, Ruby raises `TypeError`, which is not rescued and will crash the Sidekiq job. Since `RetrieveTopic` has no `sidekiq_options retry: false`, it will retry by default, creating avoidable job churn. This is a real defect introduced by the diff; validating `embed_url` is a String (or rescuing `TypeError`) would prevent it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No enqueue-time dedupe and no negative caching on the retrieve path (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15, app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:8-10, lib/topic_retriever.rb:21-33): every embed impression enqueues a job, so a page whose topic can never be imported floods the Sidekiq queue with near-duplicate jobs whose only work is a failed setnx; the 60s throttle only applies inside job execution and is set before retrieval regardless of outcome, so permanently failing URLs (404, readability-empty, fetch error) are re-fetched up to once per minute indefinitely as long as they have viewers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Plugin hook contract regression: the early `return raw` at app/models/post.rb:133 happens before `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`, so documented plugin cook-pipeline filters (link rewriting, nofollow injection, content filtering) are silently skipped for raw HTML posts with no opt-out or documentation

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` before calling `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` (app/models/post.rb). This means any plugins relying on the `:after_post_cook` hook will not run for `raw_html` posts created via `PostCreator` in `TopicEmbed.import` (cook_method set to raw_html). The finding about the hook being skipped is verifiable from the diff, but whether this is a "bug" vs. an intentional design choice (raw HTML explicitly bypassing the cooking pipeline) is not provable from the diff alone, so it’s best categorized as a significant compatibility/contract concern rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Already-shipped migration edited and given `force: true`: `create_table :top_topics, force: true` in db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 drops the table if it exists when the migration runs, violating released-migration immutability and risking silent data loss in environments where the table exists without the schema_migrations entry (partial states, restored dumps)

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`, changing `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists when the migration runs, which can cause silent data loss in cases where the table exists but the migration is rerun (e.g., inconsistent/partial migration state, restored DB dumps). This is a real, diff-introduced risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `{best: 5}` passed to TopicView (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13) is not implemented anywhere in this diff — if TopicView ignores unknown options, the /embed/best endpoint serves default/latest posts rather than 'best' ones, and the specs only verify the call signature (not that the option does anything), so it ships unverified

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/embed_controller.rb the new endpoint builds TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5}), and within this diff there is no corresponding change showing that TopicView implements/uses a :best option. The added spec (spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb) only asserts the constructor is called with {best: 5}, not that the rendered posts are actually the 'best' subset/order. Whether this is a real bug depends on existing TopicView behavior outside the diff, which cannot be verified here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed's `rss.items.each` loop has no begin/rescue around `TopicEmbed.import`, so a single bad feed item (nil field, bad URL, PostCreator failure, RecordNotUnique race) permanently poisons all feed importing — the job aborts, and with `retry: false` and hourly scheduling the next run dies on the same item, so later items are never imported; the unused `feed_key` also leaves no way to skip or flag a bad feed.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` iterates `rss.items.each` and directly does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and `TopicEmbed.import(...)` with no per-item error handling. A single malformed item (e.g., `i.content` being `nil` causing `nil.scrub` / `CGI.unescapeHTML(nil)` to raise, or `TopicEmbed.create!` raising on the unique `embed_url` index race) will raise and abort the whole job. Since the job is `sidekiq_options retry: false`, that run will fail and later items in that run won’t be imported. The `feed_key` method is indeed unused in this diff, offering no mechanism here to track/skip problematic items.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` runs the entire feed poll inline in every retrieve job with no lock: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` fetches and imports the whole feed synchronously once per unique embed_url per 60s, effectively DDoS-ing the embeddable host, racing the check-then-insert in `TopicEmbed.import` into `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` exceptions, and failing retrieve jobs on any PollFeed failure.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it synchronously calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` before attempting `fetch_http`. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs a full `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` fetch and iterates/imports all items, and there is no locking or exception handling around this call in `perform_retrieve`. As a result, every `perform_retrieve` invocation can trigger a full feed fetch/import inline, and any exception from `open`/parsing/import will bubble up and fail the retrieve job. Also, `TopicEmbed.import` uses a check-then-`create!` with a unique index on `embed_url`, so concurrent import paths (multiple retrievers / scheduled poller) can raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` with no rescue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: External feed content is stored and served as unsanitized raw HTML: the RSS path has no sanitization at all before content becomes `cooked`, the readability path whitelists tags but permits `javascript:` URLs in href/src attributes, and the feed-supplied URL is interpolated unescaped into HTML — a malicious or hijacked feed yields stored script running on the Discourse origin.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a "raw_html" cook path that bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline: `Post#cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb), and TopicEmbed imports create posts with `cook_method: ...[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). The RSS poller feeds `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` directly into `TopicEmbed.import` with no sanitization (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), yielding stored HTML/JS execution on the Discourse origin. Additionally, `imported_from` appends an `#{url}` string built via interpolation into the HTML (topic_embed.rb) and the only URL check is `/^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quote-breaking/injection characters in the URL. The readability path’s protocol handling (e.g., `javascript:`) cannot be verified from this diff, but the unsanitized raw HTML storage/rendering issue is directly evidenced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Outbound HTTP calls (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and `open(url).read`) have no explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`, no redirect policy, and no response-size cap, so a slow feed server ties up Sidekiq workers and a huge response is slurped wholesale into memory before being persisted with no post-length bound.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces outbound HTTP fetching via Ruby open-uri without any guards: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` and `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` in `app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote`. There are no explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`, no redirect control, and `open(url).read` will slurp the full response into memory. In Sidekiq jobs (`PollFeed` / `RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever` -> `import_remote`), this can tie up workers on slow/never-responding servers and risk memory blowups on large responses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `/embed/best` enqueues a `RetrieveTopic` background job on every request with no rate limiting — the Referer host check in `ensure_embeddable` is a client-controlled, trivially spoofed header, so varying the `embed_url` param generates unbounded queue growth; the 60s Redis throttle limits fetch frequency, not enqueue volume.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no existing embed is found (`topic_id` nil), the code unconditionally does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)` on every request and immediately renders `loading`—there is no server-side rate limit or de-duplication at enqueue time. The only throttle shown is in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, but that runs inside the background job (`Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute`) and therefore does not prevent unbounded job creation/queue growth; it only short-circuits the fetch after the job has already been enqueued and picked up. Additionally, `ensure_embeddable` relies on `request.referer` host matching `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, which is a client-supplied header and can be trivially spoofed, so an attacker can pass the check and spam `/embed/best?embed_url=...` to enqueue arbitrarily many jobs (and can vary `embed_url` to avoid the per-URL Redis key entirely).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No lifecycle cleanup for `topic_embeds`: nothing deletes a TopicEmbed when its topic or post is deleted, leaving a stale topic_id that makes `TopicView.new` 404, permanently blocking re-creation for that URL because `perform_retrieve` short-circuits on the existing embed, and causing a `NoMethodError` when `PostRevisor.new(post)` receives a nil post.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed` records keyed by `embed_url` (unique index) and retrieval code that short-circuits if any record exists: `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` returns early on `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`. There is no lifecycle cleanup (`dependent: :destroy` on `belongs_to` or foreign keys with cascade) for `topic_embeds` when the associated `topic`/`post` is deleted, so stale rows can remain. `EmbedController#best` uses `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` (pluck of stored `topic_id`) and then `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)`; if the topic was deleted, this can lead to a broken/404 view while also blocking re-creation because retrieval won’t run due to the existing stale embed row. Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import`’s update path does `post = embed.post` and then `PostRevisor.new(post)` if content changes; if the post was deleted, `embed.post` can be nil, causing a `NoMethodError`/crash. These failure modes are directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The embed loading page reloads forever with no failure state or retry cap, and failure is silent on both client and operator side: retrieval silently no-ops when `embed_by_username` is unset or the user was deleted, when the host doesn't match, or when retrieval fails, and no poll/retrieve path logs anything — with no circuit breaker, a permanently-bad embed URL is re-fetched once a minute indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: The new `embed/loading.html.erb` unconditionally reloads the page every 30s with no max retries or error UI. In `EmbedController#best`, when no `TopicEmbed` exists it always enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` and renders `loading`, so a never-created embed leads to infinite reloads. `TopicRetriever#retrieve` can silently do nothing: `invalid_host?` returns true if `URI(@embed_url).host` doesn’t equal `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and `fetch_http` returns if the `embed_by_username` lookup finds no user (e.g., unset/blank setting or deleted user). There’s no logging or failure state in these paths, and `retrieved_recently?` throttles retries to once per 60s, so a bad/misconfigured embed will keep being retried indefinitely while the iframe reloads forever.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feed item parsing assumes `i.content` exists, but simple-rss exposes namespaced `content:encoded` as `content_encoded`, so RSS 2.0 description-only feeds raise `NoMethodError` on `i.content.scrub`, and combined with the missing error isolation one such item kills the entire poll.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. The diff shows no nil-check or fallback (e.g., `description`, `content_encoded`), and no per-item rescue. If an item lacks `content` (or it is nil), calling `.scrub` will raise (NoMethodError), aborting the entire `poll_feed` job and preventing remaining items from being imported.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `String#scrub` requires Ruby ≥ 2.1 but these migrations are dated to the pre-Ruby-2.1 deployment era and the `string-scrub` gem was not added to the Gemfile, so on a runtime lacking it every poll raises on the first item and feed importing never works at all.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Jobs::PollFeed` which calls `i.content.scrub` (`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`). `String#scrub` is not polyfilled anywhere in the diff, and no dependency such as `string-scrub` is added to the Gemfile/lockfile. If the runtime Ruby lacks `String#scrub` (pre-2.1), feed polling would raise `NoMethodError` on the first item and break importing. The diff itself shows the risky call and lack of polyfill, but does not show what Ruby versions are supported, so impact depends on the deployment Ruby.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration `add_cook_method_to_posts` uses `ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT ... NOT NULL`, which on PostgreSQL < 11 rewrites the `posts` table while holding an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, causing minutes of total post-query lockout during deploy on busy forums.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb` that does `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions prior to 11, adding a column with a non-null default is known to require a table rewrite and take an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, which can block reads/writes on a large `posts` table during deploy. This is a deployment/performance risk rather than a functional correctness bug, but it is directly grounded in the migration shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `setnx`/`expire` throttle in `TopicRetriever` is not atomic: if the worker dies between the two calls, the `retrieved:<url>` key persists with no TTL and that URL is throttled permanently until manual Redis intervention; should use `set(key, "1", nx: true, ex: 60)`.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, `retrieved_recently?` uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or is terminated after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the `retrieved:<url>` key will remain without a TTL, causing that embed URL to be throttled indefinitely until Redis is manually cleaned. Using a single atomic `SET` with `NX` and `EX` would avoid this failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `import_remote` fetches the URL before validating its scheme: `open(url)` executes before the `^https?://` check in `import`, so a schemeless string like `//eviltrout.com/x` passes `invalid_host?` and hits `Kernel#open`'s local-file semantics instead of HTTP.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code calls `open(url).read` immediately (no scheme validation there) and only later calls `TopicEmbed.import`, which is where the `^https?://` check exists. Separately, `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` validates only `URI(@embed_url).host` against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and `URI("//eviltrout.com/x").host` is `"eviltrout.com"`, so a schemeless URL can pass host validation and reach `open(url)`. That means `open("//eviltrout.com/x")` will be treated as a local path by `Kernel#open` unless `open-uri` handling is guaranteed, matching the finding’s concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `<%- end if %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` is a typo (presumably meant `<%- end %>`) that only renders correctly by accident of ERB's chunk emission order, and is one template edit away from a semantics change or a `SyntaxError` that breaks every embed render with a topic present.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, the header block starts with `<%- if @topic_view.posts.present? %>` and has an `else`, but it closes with `<%- end if %>`. Inside an ERB Ruby chunk, `end if` with no condition is invalid Ruby syntax (Ruby only allows `begin ... end if <condition>` when a condition is present). This will cause an ERB compilation `SyntaxError` and break rendering of the embed view.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `create_table ..., force: true` in production migrations (`create_topic_embeds`, `create_top_topics`) can silently drop any pre-existing table without warning if the migration is re-run, and modifying the already-shipped `CreateTopTopics` migration is a no-op on already-migrated databases that only adds risk.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `force: true` to production migrations: `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` creates `topic_embeds` with `force: true`, and `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` changes `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop an existing table before re-creating it, which can cause silent data loss if the migration is re-run or the table already exists. Additionally, altering the already-existing `CreateTopTopics` migration won’t affect already-migrated production DBs but does increase risk for environments that may replay migrations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The Disqus import loop now performs network I/O with no rescue: `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)` inside `parser.threads.each` means a single 404 or timeout on an old export permalink aborts the entire CLI run partway through.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the import loop now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)` for each thread. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (in `app/models/topic_embed.rb`) does `open(url).read` with no error handling. `open-uri` can raise on 404s, timeouts, DNS failures, etc., so a single bad permalink would raise and abort the entire Thor CLI run mid-loop. Previously, the loop created a post without network I/O, so this is a newly introduced failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Jobs::PollFeed's core feed-to-topic pipeline has zero behavioral coverage: the spec stubs poll_feed itself, so SimpleRSS parsing, the link fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), the missing-user early return, and the handoff to TopicEmbed.import are never executed, and no test anywhere verifies a feed item produces a topic/post. This untested path hides a latent crash: i.content.scrub (poll_feed.rb:35) raises NoMethodError on feeds/items lacking a content element (common in plain RSS 2.0 feeds with only <description>), and since the job is sidekiq_options retry: false, it dies silently every hour.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the job unconditionally does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` inside `rss.items.each`. If a feed item lacks a `content` field (e.g., RSS items with only `description`), `i.content` can be nil and `nil.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, causing the scheduled job to fail. The spec (spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb) only asserts execute-gating and never exercises `poll_feed`, so this failure mode isn’t covered anywhere in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Imported HTML is served completely unsanitized: Post#cook returns raw verbatim for cook_method: raw_html, bypassing the cooking/sanitization pipeline and the Plugin::Filter :after_post_cook hooks. PollFeed passes raw feed HTML straight into this path (only the readability path whitelists tags), and the embed view renders it with raw post.cooked (and it renders unsanitized on the regular topic page too) — a crafted feed/article containing <script> or onerror= executes in the Discourse origin for every viewer, including logged-in users. The spec (topic_embed_spec.rb:29 asserting cooked == raw) codifies the vulnerability instead of guarding against it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when that cook_method is set, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization path and the `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` hook (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` using `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), and `Jobs::PollFeed` passes feed `i.content` directly into `TopicEmbed.import` after only `CGI.unescapeHTML`/`scrub` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), with no sanitization or tag/attribute whitelist. The embed template renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), and since `post.cooked` == `post.raw` for raw_html, crafted HTML (e.g., `<script>` or event handlers) would execute in the Discourse origin. The spec explicitly asserts `post.cooked.should == post.raw` for imported content (spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb), reinforcing the unsafe behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The three PollFeed guard tests (spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:12-30) pass for the wrong reason: each stubs only one setting and leaves the others at their real defaults (feed_polling_enabled: false, feed_polling_url: '', embed_by_username: '') which already make the poll_feed condition false — e.g. 'requires feed_polling_url' leaves feed_polling_enabled? at default false so the first conjunct short-circuits. Deleting any single gating condition would not fail any spec; each test should set the other two settings to valid values so only the condition under test can fail.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb the three guard tests each stub only one of the three conjunctive conditions used in Jobs::PollFeed#execute (feed_polling_enabled? && feed_polling_url.present? && embed_by_username.present?). The other two settings remain at their defaults from config/site_settings.yml (feed_polling_enabled: false, feed_polling_url: '', embed_by_username: ''), which already make the overall condition false. For example, the 'requires feed_polling_url' test stubs feed_polling_url to nil but leaves feed_polling_enabled? at default false, so the guard short-circuits regardless of the feed_polling_url check; deleting any single conjunct would not necessarily fail these tests. This is a real, diff-grounded test weakness, not a production behavior bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Every meaningful behavior of TopicRetriever is mocked in its own spec: all tests stub either perform_retrieve or retrieved_recently?, so the only real code exercised is the host comparison. The 60-second $redis.setnx/expire throttle and perform_retrieve's logic (bail if embed exists, run Jobs::PollFeed first when enabled, fetch_http's user lookup) have no coverage — a typo in the redis key, a dropped expire, or removing the exists?-check would not fail any spec.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb the tests only assert whether perform_retrieve is invoked, and in the “valid host” context they stub retrieved_recently? to true/false, so neither retrieved_recently?’s $redis.setnx/expire throttle logic nor perform_retrieve’s internal behavior (TopicEmbed.exists? bail-out, Jobs::PollFeed execution when feed_polling_enabled?, and fetch_http’s user lookup/import) is exercised. EmbedController spec also mocks TopicRetriever.new and retriever.retrieve, providing no additional coverage for this new logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The embed controller's success-path tests verify mock interactions, not behavior: 'Tells the topic retriever to work' asserts TopicRetriever.new/retrieve are called instead of asserting Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) args, and TopicRetriever.expects(:new) matches any arguments; 'Creates a topic view' mocks TopicView.new returning nil. With view rendering off, nothing verifies the best template renders posts or that the loading template renders on the no-embed path — a broken template (e.g. @topic_view.posts on a stale/deleted topic id) ships green. No render_views/integration spec exists for either new template.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, the no-topic-id path enqueues a job (`Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: ...)`) and never instantiates `TopicRetriever`. However, the new controller spec `"tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found"` expects `TopicRetriever.new` and `retriever.retrieve` to be called. This is a concrete mismatch between the diff’s implementation and its tests and would cause the spec to fail (and it also does not assert the actual behavior: `Jobs.enqueue` with correct args).

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import_remote has no tests despite becoming the backbone of TopicRetriever#fetch_http and the rewritten disqus importer (disqus.thor switched from PostCreator to TopicEmbed.import_remote): readability extraction (title extraction, tag/attribute whitelist, opts[:title] override) is never exercised, nor is failure handling — open(url) on a 404 raises inside the job with nothing asserting behavior. Any bug in extraction now silently breaks two features.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (TopicEmbed model) and makes it the primary path for remote retrieval: `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)` and `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` switches from `PostCreator` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. Specs added cover `TopicRetriever` and `TopicEmbed.import`, but none exercise `import_remote`’s Readability parsing/whitelists or `opts[:title]` override, and `open(url).read` has no rescue path—so behavior on HTTP errors (e.g., 404) isn’t specified/tested. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test/robustness gap, not a proven functional defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: 'is 404 without an embed_url' (embed_controller_spec.rb:8-11) never reaches params.require and passes for the wrong reason: with no stub, the real default embeddable_host is '' so ensure_embeddable raises before the action runs — the loose should_not be_success passes because of the blank host (and the status is 403, not 404). Deleting params.require(:embed_url) would not fail any test.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController`, `before_filter :ensure_embeddable` runs before `best`, and `ensure_embeddable` raises if `SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank?` (new default in `config/site_settings.yml` is `embeddable_host: ''`). In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the example `it "is 404 without an embed_url" do; get :best; response.should_not be_success; end` does not stub `embeddable_host` or set a referer, so it will fail early in `ensure_embeddable` and never exercise `params.require(:embed_url)` inside `best`. As written, the test would still pass even if `params.require(:embed_url)` were removed, so it’s a real, diff-grounded gap/misleading test rather than a production defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The TopicEmbed update test cannot detect if revision loses raw_html cooking: post.cooked =~ /new contents/ would also pass if PostRevisor cooked the new raw through the regular markdown pipeline (the phrase survives markdown), so nothing verifies cook_method is preserved across revision. Also untested: importing identical content triggers no revision (the content_sha1 guard and embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...)), and that update doesn't create a duplicate topic/embed (TopicEmbed.count == 1 never asserted).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new behavior around `cook_method` (creation sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in `TopicEmbed.import`, and `Post#cook` bypasses cooking when `raw_html`). On update, `TopicEmbed.import` revises the existing post via `PostRevisor#revise!` without explicitly asserting that `cook_method` remains `:raw_html`. The spec `"Supports updating the post"` only checks `post.cooked =~ /new contents/`, which would still pass even if the post were re-cooked via the normal pipeline, so it doesn’t meaningfully test the raw_html preservation. Similarly, there is no test asserting the SHA1 guard prevents revision when content is unchanged, nor that repeated imports keep `TopicEmbed.count` at 1 and don’t create duplicate topics/embeds. These are concrete, diff-grounded test gaps for newly added logic, not a demonstrated runtime defect in the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls edge cases are untested, including a real mangling of protocol-relative URLs: //cdn.example.com/x starts with /, gets all leading slashes stripped by sub(/^\/+/, ''), and is rewritten to http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/x — a common real-world pattern that silently produces broken links. Port-bearing URLs (prefix << ":#{uri.port}") are also uncovered.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, any `href`/`src` that `start_with?('/')` is rewritten via `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`. For protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x`, this strips both leading slashes and rewrites to something like `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/x`, silently breaking valid external links. The added spec only covers single-slash relative paths (`/hello`, `/images/...`) and does not cover this real-world case (nor port-bearing prefixes), so the defect is both present and untested.
