adjudication_records.issue_text: `force: true` in the new create_topic_embeds migration (db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3) gives destructive drop-if-exists semantics with no protection for pre-existing data: on MySQL (non-transactional DDL) a re-run after a partial failure, or any re-run against a database that already has `topic_embeds` rows, silently drops the table and its data

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` (db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb), which in Rails issues a drop-if-exists before creating the table. If this migration is re-run (e.g., after a partial failure or on an environment where the table already exists), it can silently drop `topic_embeds` and all rows, matching the finding’s data-loss concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `add_column :posts, :cook_method` with NOT NULL DEFAULT (db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3) triggers a full table rewrite of the hottest, largest table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on PostgreSQL < 11 and MySQL of this era, blocking all reads/writes to `posts` for a potentially minutes-long rewrite on large forums (no `disable_ddl_transaction!` or staged add-then-backfill-then-constrain approach)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` (db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb). On large `posts` tables, adding a NOT NULL column with a DEFAULT in older PostgreSQL/MySQL commonly triggers a full table rewrite and requires strong locking (potentially blocking reads/writes). The migration is not staged (add nullable -> backfill -> add constraint/default) and does not use any online/DDL-safety patterns (e.g., `disable_ddl_transaction!`). This is a concrete operational risk grounded in the diff, but not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `Kernel#open` is called on the admin-editable `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29) and on `url` in app/models/topic_embed.rb:34; strings beginning with `|` execute as shell commands, so a site setting value like `| <cmd>` runs arbitrary commands as the app user on the next hourly poll — non-http(s) schemes should be rejected

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` (after `require 'open-uri'`). In Ruby, `Kernel#open` supports pipe execution (e.g., `open("| cmd")`) and `open-uri` does not remove that behavior, so an admin-editable setting like `feed_polling_url` could trigger command execution if set to a string starting with `|`. Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` on `url` without enforcing an http(s) scheme before the `open`, so a `| ...` value there would also be dangerous if reachable. This is a concrete security defect grounded in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Neither the feed fetch (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29) nor the article fetch (app/models/topic_embed.rb:34) sets an `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`, so an unresponsive feed or article host can wedge Sidekiq workers indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows both network fetches use Ruby's `open-uri` without explicit timeouts: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` and `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` in `app/models/topic_embed.rb`. That’s a concrete reliability concern for Sidekiq jobs because a slow/hung remote host can tie up a worker longer than desired. However, the finding’s claim that it can wedge workers "indefinitely" isn’t strictly verifiable from the diff alone because it depends on Ruby/Net::HTTP defaults and OS-level timeouts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `--category` CLI option was removed outright from lib/tasks/disqus.thor (~line 117) with no deprecation, so existing import invocations now fail with an unknown-option error

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and also deletes the code that reads `options[:category]` and passes a `category:` id into `PostCreator`. With Thor, removing a declared option means invocations that still pass `--category`/`-c` will now raise an unknown option error. This is a backwards-incompatible CLI change (likely intentional due to switching to `TopicEmbed.import_remote`), but it’s not a defect in application correctness per se—it's an API/CLI compatibility concern without deprecation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The Disqus thor import no longer propagates `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` or the category, so imported topics are created uncategorized with current timestamps instead of their original post dates — a permanent data-quality regression for anyone re-running the import

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the previous import path created the topic via `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` (and supported `--category`). The diff removes the `:category` option entirely and replaces topic creation with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which ultimately calls `PostCreator.new(user, title: ..., raw: ..., skip_validations: true, cook_method: ...)` in `TopicEmbed.import` without passing `created_at` or any category. From the diff alone, this means imported topics will use current timestamps and default category (likely uncategorized), matching the finding’s claimed regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No cleanup or state handling exists for `TopicEmbed` rows whose topic or post is deleted: nothing deletes the rows when their topic/post is destroyed, `topic_id_for_embed` does not filter deleted topics, and the update path assumes `embed.post` exists, so embed requests for that URL 500 (TopicView on a missing topic) or serve the deleted topic, and the next feed poll runs `PostRevisor.new(post)` on a missing/deleted post, crashing the job

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed` as a separate table linked to `topics`/`posts` (migration `create_topic_embeds`, model `belongs_to :topic` / `belongs_to :post`) but adds no cleanup (`dependent: ...`, callbacks, or FK constraints). `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` blindly plucks `topic_id` by `embed_url` without checking that the referenced topic still exists. In the update path of `TopicEmbed.import`, it does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally constructs `PostRevisor.new(post)` if the content changed; if the associated post has been removed, `embed.post` will be `nil` and this will raise. Similarly, `EmbedController#best` will call `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` on a potentially non-existent topic id returned by `topic_id_for_embed`, which can 500. These are concrete crash paths stemming from missing state handling for orphaned `topic_embeds`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test suite mocks out every boundary in the PR — controller specs never render views, poll_feed_spec stubs poll_feed itself, retriever specs stub perform_retrieve — so the suite stays green while multiple real paths are broken or unsafe (the poll_feed body is never executed in CI)

adjudication.rationale: The new specs do largely stub/mocks away the core behavior they’re meant to validate. In `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`, the only positive-path test for `execute` sets `poller.expects(:poll_feed).once`, which prevents the real `poll_feed` implementation (the RSS fetch/parse/import loop in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`) from ever running under test. Similarly, `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` stubs `perform_retrieve`/`retrieved_recently?` and asserts call/no-call rather than exercising retrieval logic (RSS polling + HTTP fetch) in `lib/topic_retriever.rb`. `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` is a controller spec without `render_views`, so it won’t render the new embed templates. This is a concrete coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic, but it’s not itself a verifiable runtime defect from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — the stray '<%- end if %>' is a Ruby syntax error: the template has 4 block opens (header if l.2, stray if l.6, posts if l.11, each do l.12) but only 3 ends, so ERB fails to compile and every /embed/best request that finds an existing topic returns a 500 — the feature's primary path is dead on arrival, silently passing because controller specs don't render templates

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/embed/best.html.erb the header block starts with `<%- if @topic_view.posts.present? %>` / `<%- else %>` but is closed with `<%- end if %>`. `end if` without a trailing condition is invalid Ruby syntax in ERB and will cause the template to fail to compile; it should be `<%- end %>`. This is a real runtime failure on the /embed/best path that renders this template (and controller specs shown don’t enable view rendering).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: imported feed/fetched HTML is cooked and stored with zero sanitization (post.rb:131 cook returns raw unchanged for raw_html and skips the after_post_cook plugin filter; no sanitizer or readability whitelist in topic_embed.rb:22/35-37 or poll_feed.rb:35-36; skip_validations: true bypasses the normal pipeline) and is rendered raw via '<%= raw post.cooked %>' in embed/best.html.erb:19 and on the forum topic page — since the embed iframe is served from the Discourse origin with the viewer's cookies, any injected script executes with full session access, including admin sessions

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a raw-HTML path that bypasses Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization: Post#cook now returns `raw` unchanged when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb), and TopicEmbed.import creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `skip_validations: true` using RSS/remote contents (app/models/topic_embed.rb). The RSS path (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) passes `i.content` through `CGI.unescapeHTML` but does not sanitize/whitelist tags/attributes before storing. The embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), so any injected HTML/JS in imported content will execute in the Discourse origin context. This is a verifiable stored XSS risk introduced/exposed by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:36-38 asserts post.cooked == post.raw, enshrining the unsanitized passthrough as intended behavior

adjudication.rationale: The spec assertion is accurate: `Post#cook` now returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb), and `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` from RSS/remote content (app/models/topic_embed.rb, app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). That means imported HTML bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline, and the embed view renders it with `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), creating an XSS risk from feed/page content. The test (`post.cooked.should == post.raw`) effectively locks in this unsafe passthrough behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — the embed URL is interpolated unescaped into the 'imported from' footer #{url}; quotes are legal URI characters, so an embed_url like http://host/x'onclick='…' passes URI parsing and the host check, injects attributes, survives absolutize_urls' Nokogiri round-trip, and is stored and rendered raw

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends `contents << "... #{url} ..."` using the unescaped `url` (only guarded by `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`). Imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly for `:raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view renders `raw post.cooked`, so any quote/attribute-breaking characters in `url` would be persisted and rendered as raw HTML, enabling attribute/HTML injection/XSS via a crafted `embed_url`/feed link.

adjudication_records.issue_text: javascript: hrefs from readability's href-whitelisted output (topic_embed.rb:49-50) pass through to rendered imported content — same class of injection as the unescaped footer URL

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, Readability is configured to allow `a` tags and the `href` attribute (`tags: %w[... a img]`, `attributes: %w[href src]`). The resulting `doc.content` is then imported via `TopicEmbed.import` into a post created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged for `:raw_html`. The embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. There is no sanitization or scheme validation on `href`, so a `javascript:` (or similar) URL in `href` could pass through and be rendered, creating an XSS/injection defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: /embed/best is an unauthenticated fetch/job/topic-creation amplifier (embed_controller.rb:15,26): the Referer check is client-controlled and trivially forged, RetrieveTopic is enqueued on every GET cache miss with no rate limit at enqueue time, the throttle is per-URL only (60s), bypassed entirely for staff, with no bound on distinct URLs — an attacker can flood Sidekiq, make the server fetch unlimited URLs, and create unlimited topics via skip_validations plus bypass_rate_limiter for any path returning 200

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds a public `GET /embed/best` endpoint (`routes.rb`, `EmbedController#best`) that, on cache miss (`TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` returns nil), unconditionally enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (`embed_controller.rb`), with no enqueue-time rate limiting. Access control in `ensure_embeddable` relies on `request.referer` host equality (`URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`), but the Referer header is client-supplied and can be forged, so an attacker can hit the endpoint directly. The job-side throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is only per-URL (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}` for 60s) and does not bound distinct URLs, so an attacker can vary `embed_url` paths on the allowed host to generate unlimited queued jobs and corresponding outbound fetches (`TopicEmbed.import_remote(open(url).read)`) and topic/post creations (`PostCreator` with `skip_validations: true`). This is an amplification / DoS vector introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RetrieveTopic does not set retry: false (unlike PollFeed), so poison URLs that raise in the job are re-fetched repeatedly by Sidekiq's default retry policy

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Jobs::PollFeed` explicitly sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, but the newly added `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb) does not set any `sidekiq_options`. Its `execute` method can raise (e.g., `Discourse::InvalidParameters` when `embed_url` missing, and `TopicRetriever#retrieve` ultimately calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `open(url).read` without rescue). With Sidekiq's default retry behavior, such failures could be retried repeatedly, potentially re-fetching a bad/poison URL. This is an operational robustness concern grounded in the added code, but not a guaranteed functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: open(url) at topic_embed.rb:48 follows redirects, so the host check in TopicRetriever does not actually constrain what gets fetched — one open redirect on the embeddable host hands the attacker control of the imported HTML, feeding the XSS/URL-injection issues

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, the only constraint is `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`, which validates only the original URL’s host. But `TopicEmbed.import_remote` then does `open(url).read` (open-uri) which will follow HTTP redirects by default. Therefore a URL on the allowed `embeddable_host` that 30x-redirects to another host can cause Discourse to fetch and import content from an attacker-controlled destination, bypassing the intended host restriction shown in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31-37 — no per-item rescue in the items.each loop means one poison item kills the whole poll permanently: with retry: false and stable feed order it dies at the same item every hour and everything after it is never imported; ordinary triggers include nil i.content for RSS 2.0 items (they use description; simple-rss returns nil) causing NoMethodError, and nil i.title causing a DB not-null violation under skip_validations

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (line ~35). If an RSS item lacks `content` (common for RSS 2.0 where `description` is used), `i.content` can be `nil`, causing `NoMethodError` on `scrub` and aborting the entire poll run. There is no per-item rescue, and the job is `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so each scheduled execution can repeatedly fail on the same poison item and prevent importing subsequent items in the feed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: String#scrub (poll_feed.rb:35) requires Ruby 2.1+ — on the Ruby 2.0 runtime contemporary with these lockfiles, every feed item crashes the poll

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`. `String#scrub` is a core Ruby method that is not available on older Rubies (e.g., 2.0/1.9), and there is no compatibility shim shown in the diff. If this app is run on such a runtime, polling a feed will raise `NoMethodError` for every item and break the job.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:35 double entity-decodes feed content: CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) on simple-rss output that is already decoded turns legitimately escaped text like '<script>' into live markup (feeding the stored XSS) and corrupts ordinary &…; text

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then passes that into `TopicEmbed.import(...)`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly for `raw_html`, meaning the imported feed HTML bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. Therefore, unescaping entities like `<script>` into `<script>` would be stored and later rendered as live markup (e.g., via `raw post.cooked` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`), which is a verifiable stored-XSS risk / content corruption introduced by this diff. The specific claim that SimpleRSS output is "already decoded" can't be confirmed from the diff, but the unsafe unescape+raw_html behavior is visible here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:35-46 — the full feed poll runs synchronously inside the per-request job (Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) is invoked inline); any feed exception aborts perform_retrieve before fetch_http, so enabling feed polling with a broken feed silently disables direct embedding too

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline and does not rescue any exceptions. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` uses `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and `SimpleRSS.parse`, either of which can raise; if that happens, `perform_retrieve` will abort before reaching `fetch_http`, preventing direct HTTP embedding when the feed is broken.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key (poll_feed.rb:20-22) is dead code — the intended feed-modified check was never wired up, so every first-time embed request re-downloads and re-processes the entire feed

adjudication.rationale: `Jobs::PollFeed` defines `feed_key` (poll_feed.rb:20-22) but never uses it; there is no conditional check (e.g., Redis/Last-Modified/ETag) to avoid re-fetching. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`, which in turn calls `poll_feed` and unconditionally does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all items. This can cause repeated full-feed downloads on embed retrieval paths, but it’s primarily an efficiency/incomplete-wiring issue rather than a correctness defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent permanent-failure loop: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 reloads every 30s forever with no failure state, fetch_http returns silently when embed_by_username is unset or the user is missing (topic_retriever.rb:49-52), failed fetches are not negatively cached, and the job's only outcomes are nil — no error ever surfaces to admin or viewer

adjudication.rationale: The new loading view unconditionally reloads the page every 30s (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:7-11). If the embed cannot be retrieved/created, the controller will keep rendering this loading page because TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed stays nil (EmbedController#best). TopicRetriever#fetch_http returns early with no error when the configured embed user is missing/blank (lib/topic_retriever.rb:49-52), so no TopicEmbed is created and no failure is surfaced; the user experiences an indefinite reload loop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic throttle in topic_retriever.rb:27-28: $redis.setnx followed by a separate expire — a crash between them leaves the retrieved:<url> key with no TTL, permanently pinning that URL as 'recently retrieved' so it is never fetched again

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb retrieved_recently? uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then calls `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` in a separate command. If the process crashes or loses connectivity after setnx succeeds but before expire executes, the `retrieved:<url>` key will persist without a TTL. Subsequent calls will see setnx fail and return `true` (treated as "retrieved recently"), preventing `perform_retrieve` indefinitely for that URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:4 references stylesheet_link_tag 'embed' but nothing registers embed.css for asset precompilation (no config.assets.precompile entry), so Rails 4 production serves 404/unstyled embeds while dev and the non-rendering specs stay green

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new standalone stylesheet (app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss) and references it via stylesheet_link_tag 'embed' in app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb, but the finding’s key assertion—"nothing registers embed.css for asset precompilation (no config.assets.precompile entry)"—cannot be verified from this diff because no asset precompile configuration (e.g., config/initializers/assets.rb) or existing manifest requirements are shown. From the diff alone, we can’t conclude it will 404 in Rails 4 production.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:21-30 — PostCreator (which enqueues follow-up Sidekiq jobs immediately) runs inside an open Topic.transaction; those workers can run before commit and miss rows, or operate on rolled-back post IDs, causing orphaned/phantom jobs and intermittent missing post-processing (search indexing, tracking) with no error to the user

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicEmbed.import` wrapping `PostCreator.new(...).create` inside `Topic.transaction`, but it does not show (or change) any behavior where `PostCreator` “enqueues follow-up Sidekiq jobs immediately.” The only `PostCreator` change in this PR is setting `post.cook_method` from opts, with no job enqueue logic visible. Therefore the claimed race (workers running before commit/rolled-back IDs) is not verifiable from this diff and is speculative given the provided evidence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dup-import TOCTOU race: two concurrent retrievals can both pass the exists?/where(embed_url:).first checks (topic_retriever.rb:37, topic_embed.rb:15), and the loser explodes on the unique index and rolls back

adjudication.rationale: The diff implements a classic check-then-insert flow around a unique key without handling concurrent inserts. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` it first does `return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` and then later calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`TopicEmbed.import`. In `TopicEmbed.import`, it does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank enters a transaction and calls `TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url, ...)`, while the migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`. Two concurrent retrieval/imports for the same `embed_url` can both observe “no row”, then both attempt `create!`; the loser will raise (e.g., `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`) and roll back. There is no rescue/retry/upsert logic shown, so this can explode jobs/requests under concurrency (including PollFeed vs RetrieveTopic).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:18 — postMessage origin is 'validated' by substring match (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1), which both admits imposters (any substring-matching origin) and drops legitimate messages (trailing-slash/protocol mismatch means resize is never applied; with scrolling='no' and no default height, comments are permanently clipped)
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate flags the same core security issue: validating postMessage origins via a substring/indexOf check is unsafe and can be bypassed by attacker-controlled domains that contain the trusted domain as a substring (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com). It also notes additional side effects, but the underlying vulnerability matches the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js — e.data.height is never type-checked before being assigned via iframe.height = e.data.height + 'px'

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `iframe.height = e.data.height + "px"` without explicit numeric type-checking (app/assets/javascripts/embed.js). However, the only sender shown in this diff is the embed iframe itself (layouts/embed.html.erb), which posts `document.body.offsetHeight` (a number). Given the intended message format in the diff, lack of extra type-checking does not constitute a verifiable defect introduced by this change; at worst it’s a minor hardening suggestion rather than a clear bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:8-11 — iframe height is computed once at window.onload, before avatars/logo load; late images change the height after the single postMessage, leaving an undersized iframe that clips posts

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb the resize message is sent from `window.onload`, which fires only after the document and its dependent resources (including `` elements like avatars/logo) have finished loading. The diff does not show any subsequent dynamic insertion of images/content after `onload` that would increase height, so the claim that late-loading images will change height after the single postMessage is not supported by the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:8-11 — targetOrigin is bound to request.referer, so any parent whose actual origin differs from the Referer (redirects, mirrors) silently never receives the resize
matched_golden_ids: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag that using request.referer (a full URL that may include path/query and can differ due to redirects/mirrors) as postMessage targetOrigin can mismatch the parent origin, causing the message to be dropped and resize to fail. This is the same underlying issue: targetOrigin should be just the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:65,71 — absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs: '//cdn.com/x.jpg' matches start_with?('/') and the leading-slash strip removes both slashes, producing http://eviltrout.com/cdn.com/x.jpg — silently broken images/links for a common feed pattern

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, both link and image rewrites check `start_with?('/')` and then do `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` (and same for `src`). Protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.com/x.jpg` satisfy `start_with?('/')`, and the `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both leading slashes, producing `cdn.com/x.jpg`, which is then prefixed with the origin (e.g. `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.com/x.jpg`).
